# fjordrun_ssh_key (Resource)

A public SSH key on your account, accepted by the SFTP and SSH servers you start. Keys are personal, so this needs a personal access token: team API tokens can't manage them. The API can't change a key: every attribute replaces it, and removing a key stops the servers started with it.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Needs a personal access token: SSH keys belong to you, not to a team.
resource "fjordrun_ssh_key" "laptop" {
  name       = "work laptop"
  public_key = "ssh-ed25519 AAAAC3NzaC1lZDI1NTE5AAAAIGw8mYD6vVpC8Hvzq1gq0p2yA3qXv7XyW9m0qkZQwT4V ana@laptop"
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) A name for the key (1-100 characters).
- `public_key` (String) The public key, in `authorized_keys` format: `ssh-ed25519`, `ecdsa-sha2-nistp256/384/521`, or `ssh-rsa` with 3072 bits or more. The API doesn't return it, so an imported key is checked against `fingerprint`.

### Read-Only

- `created_at` (String) Creation time.
- `fingerprint` (String) SHA256 fingerprint, as `ssh-keygen -lf` prints it.
- `id` (String) Key ID.
- `key_type` (String) Key type.
- `last_used_at` (String) Last login to a server with this key.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# by key ID. The API doesn't return the public key: the next apply takes it from your configuration, if the fingerprint matches.
terraform import fjordrun_ssh_key.laptop ffffffff-ffff-ffff-ffff-ffffffffffff
```
